title: Radioactive Waste Half-Life
learningObjectives: Explain that half of the remaining radioactivity decays during each half-life period
Calculate the amount remaining after a given time using the half-life equation
Compare the 30-year half-lives of cesium-137 and strontium-90 with the 24,000-year half-life of plutonium-239

evidence.quote: Radioactive isotopes eventually decay, or disintegrate, to harmless materials.

explanations.text: Radioactive isotopes decay over time to harmless materials, with some decaying quickly and others very slowly.

evidence.quote: Strontium-90 and cesium-137 have half-lives of about 30 years (half the radioactivity will decay in 30 years).

explanations.text: Strontium-90 and cesium-137 have half-lives of about 30 years, so half the radioactivity decays every 30 years.

evidence.quote: Plutonium-239 has a half-life of 24,000 years.
Transuranic wastes, sometimes called TRU, account for most of the radioactive hazard remaining in high-level waste after 1,000 years.

explanations.text: Plutonium-239 has a 24,000-year half-life, so transuranic waste accounts for most remaining hazard after 1,000 years.
